summary: The Software Factory as its own first customer: two disposable labs it already owns, one backlog/improvement target and one defect target, staging-only, budget-capped, Owner-stoppable.
rollback_criteria: a staging deployment fails its health check
an improvement candidate regresses a non-regression metric
a repair mission reopens the incident it closed
the acceptance digest of a frozen artifact moves without a supersession
stop_conditions: the run budget ceiling is reached
any duplicate irreversible provider effect is observed
three consecutive cycles end in infrastructure failure for every project
the Owner engages the portfolio emergency stop

productization_gate.rationale: Every threshold retires a specific risk that the current evidence does not retire, and each number is chosen from what has actually been measured rather than from a round figure. The Stage-9 campaign covered 288 cycles of virtual time, four simulated projects and zero cycles of real host time; the one real end-to-end mission on record (FLM-1) reached a provider through a path whose dispatch leg was a fixture. So the sustained-operation numbers are stated in real host cycles and real days, and the execution numbers are stated in missions that reached a provider process. 2016 cycles is seven days at the contract's 300-second interval: the shortest span that necessarily contains a host sleep/wake, a reboot and a weekly rhythm. 20 real missions is the smallest sample in which a 5% failure rate makes at least one failure expected rather than surprising, which is what makes a zero-failure result meaningful. Two projects is the minimum at which cross-project isolation is a claim about the mechanism and not about the only project there was. Zero is used only where a single instance falsifies a safety property outright -- duplicate irreversible effects, authority bypass, isolation violations, gate-provenance violations -- because for those a ratio would be a tolerance nobody decided to grant. 0.95 for cost accounting rather than 1.0 because a provider that returns no usage block is a reported-claim absence the Factory records honestly as not_measurable, and refusing to productize over a provider's telemetry gap would put the gate on the wrong party. Four Owner control acts is the whole control surface -- pause, drain, emergency stop, clear -- each proven against the real host rather than a store.
